headline: Nasdaq-100 ends quadruple-witching week at 29,644.17, up 0.67% at the top of its range, and the weekend futures halt removes the tradable path
body: NDX settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, inside a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range after opening at 29,529.64 against a 29,447.00 prior close. The close landed near the session high, which in isolation is the classic holding-near-extremes signal, but the shape of the day argues the other way: price first sold off roughly 0.53% from the open to 29,371.89 and then retraced the full move and extended. Retracements completed rather than failed, which is the opposite of the pathological no-pullback path, and the closing push coincided with a quadruple-witching expiration that concentrated settlement flow into the 20:00Z print. Volatility agreed: VIX closed at 14.81, down about 4.1% and near its 14.80 session low, versus a 17.71 prior close. Cross-assets stayed split rather than aligned. The 10-year Treasury yield ended the week near 5.00% after touching 5.041% earlier in the week, its highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.67% on the latest H.15 column, following the Federal Reserve's 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September in a 12-0 vote and projections pointing to a further move; futures price roughly two-in-three odds of a hike on 28 October. Crude fell for a third session, with WTI down about 2.3% to $99.54 and Brent $103.22, as markets judged the shut Saudi East-West pipeline less damaging than first feared and Saudi Arabia worked to restore roughly half its capacity within days. The geopolitical backdrop remains live: Iran's IRGC said it struck the Togo-flagged tanker Trend in the Strait of Hormuz and warned that unauthorised passage would meet destruction. Semiconductors recovered into the close after the mid-week AI-slowdown selloff, and the PHLX index finished the week slightly higher. The decisive factor for this assessment is mechanical rather than interpretive: CME equity-index futures closed for the week at 21:00Z and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, beyond the end of this forecast window. With no venue open, mean-reversion failure has no mechanism, so Tail falls to a residual 11 that reflects unpriced weekend gap exposure only. Stress at 33 carries the environment a reopen would face - 5% yields, a hawkish Fed path, a war-driven energy market - rather than any live drawdown path, and Confidence at 87 reflects a complete evidence set for a closed market.

lookbackSummary: The window opened on Thursday evening after the 16 September Fed hike with a trend-up mode and Tail at 20, the only hour of the 24 that mapped to WATCH. Tail eased to 17-18 overnight as the mode normalised through the Asian session, with Stress drifting from 44 down to 40 and back toward 50 into the European morning as yields firmed. The mode turned trend-up from 07:00Z, then shifted to mixed at 11:00Z once the US cash session traded two-sided, and Tail held a narrow 15-18 band for the rest of the day while Stress peaked at 51 around the 14:00-15:00Z hours. The final hour of the window carried the quadruple-witching cash close at Tail 16 and Stress 44 with a trend-up mode. Every hour from 22:00Z onward mapped to EA_ON, and no hour in the window produced the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures.
outlookSummary: The current hour is already inside the weekly halt: CME equity-index futures closed at 21:00Z and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, which falls outside this 24-hour horizon. Every one of the 24 forecast slots therefore contains no tradable NQ or NAS100 price path, and the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Forecast Tail sits at a residual 9-13, rising only gradually as the distance to the reopen shortens and unpriced weekend headlines accumulate, while Stress runs 25-33 to describe the environment a reopen would face rather than any live drawdown path. Confidence eases from 87 to 79 across the window as the marked levels age without price discovery. The dominant mode is held at normal for every slot, because a halted venue has no directional character to measure and Friday's close must not be carried forward as observed structure. The live unresolved variables into Monday are the Strait of Hormuz conflict, the Saudi East-West pipeline repair, the 10-year near 5.00% and October hike pricing; none can express before the reopen.
